brief.headline: Ask for ₹32.69 L annual savings by matching the ₹290.00/KG benchmark we already pay Shrinath Roto Pack on key laminates

priceAsk.summary: Match our best laminate price of ₹290.00/KG on the top three SKUs where they overprice by 1.4% to 6.3%
priceAsk.target: ₹32.69 L annual saving by closing the gap to our best price
priceAsk.basis: We pay Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd ₹290.00/KG for comparable laminates; GEEP charges ₹294.03/KG to ₹308.30/KG on the same material. The BOPET film import benchmark sits at 171.60 ₹/kg, well below their pricing.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt—do not concede longer terms
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹2.33 Cr working capital at risk if we move from current 30-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: GEEP's margins are razor-thin: 1.1% net vs 2.1% peer median, and 1.7% EBITDA. Their 0.57x debt-to-equity and 4.12x interest coverage are manageable, but the CRISIL BB+ / Stable rating sits on an 'Issuer Not Cooperating' flag, so their real health is uncertain. We represent 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr revenue—a meaningful ₹28.31 Cr anchor customer. Their 81d cash-conversion cycle runs 35 days longer than the 46d peer median, so they need cash velocity. Push hard on price to our benchmark; their thin 1.1% margin means a deep cut risks supply stability, so frame the ask as 'meet the market or lose volume to our alternates.' Leverage our 9.72% share and their stretched working capital, but watch the margin floor.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹32.69 L per year versus the best laminate price we already secure elsewhere
On SKU LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 08, GEEP charges ₹308.30/KG while Shrinath delivers at ₹290.00/KG—a 6.3% gap costing us ₹8.33 L annually
GEEP's net margin of 1.1% trails the 2.1% peer median, limiting room for price cuts without risking their solvency
Our ₹28.31 Cr annual spend equals 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr revenue—we are a top-tier customer
Their 81d cash-conversion cycle is 35 days slower than the 46d peer median, signaling working-capital pressure we can exploit
GEEP's CRISIL BB+ / Stable rating is marked 'Issuer Not Cooperating,' meaning the assessment is stale and financial risk is opaque

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC—proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant handling both film substrate and conversion; can absorb GEEP volume at scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India arm specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates—strong GEEP replacement

risks: GEEP supplies 67% of our laminates (₹28.31 Cr); pushing too hard without a qualified alternate risks a supply squeeze
Their 1.1% net margin leaves little cushion—demand more than a few percentage points and they may walk or cut quality
CRISIL BB+ / Stable on 'Issuer Not Cooperating' basis means their true financial health is a black box; GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases add execution risk
Current 30-day terms already tie up ₹2.33 Cr working capital; any concession to longer payment frees their cash at our expense
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹32.69 L more per year than our best laminate price—let's close that gap to ₹290.00/KG and keep this volume with you.
